freezable_call.reasoning: H1 FY26 licensing was 16.0m; underlying FY26 ex-5.9m terminations ~27.0m. Clearing 22.0m needs +37% on the comparable half. Nothing dated in the Jun-Nov-2026 window; forward book is 11.5m of 12-month receivables with only 2.5m of new fixed income signed all of FY26 (vs 11.1m). Residual 25% is a single large signing minimum-guarantee, recognised up front - the exact event that would falsify the court's central finding.

edge_explainer: SEED THESIS: 'the Warhammer franchise heat is real and GAW is the royalty carrier.' Legs 1 and 2 CONFIRM - Total War: WH40K #7, Dawn of War IV #17, Dark Heresy #30 of 5,204 unreleased Steam titles, and GAW collects on all of them at a 90.9% licensing operating margin (licensing opex 3.0m flat on 32.9m revenue). Leg 3 REFUTES and that is the court: the carry is immaterial. Calibrating off the FY24->FY25 step (+21.5m of GAW licensing revenue from Space Marine 2, the best-selling Warhammer game ever at ~7m units), the ENTIRE visible pipeline is worth 10-22m of peak-year incremental revenue = 30.8p of EPS at 15m = +250-370p capitalised honestly as a 1-2 year pulse (8-12x, which the disclosed sawtooth series 11.3/16.8/16.3/28.0/25.4/31.0/52.5/32.9 proves it is) = 1.3-1.9% of a 19,080p share; +4.9% even if wrongly capitalised at the trailing 30.6x as an annuity. Meanwhile every LEADING licensing metric GAW discloses is down: fixed income signed 11.1m->2.5m (-77%), 12-month receivables 16.4m->11.5m (-30%), total licensing receivables 24.3m->15.5m (-36%), two licensees terminated (the 5.9m of final contractual payments inside the reported 32.9m means underlying licensing is ~27.0m, BELOW FY24's 31.0m). CEO verbatim: the backdrop 'still remains challenging'; the FY27 priority is 'to sign a few significant licensing deals' - i.e. not yet signed. AND THE CORE IS DECELERATING, which no headline shows: subtracting the H1 interim from the FY26 full year gives H2 core revenue +5.1% (H1 +17.3%), H2 core operating profit +4.7% (H1 +28.5%), H2 EPS 304.1p vs 306.0p = -0.6%. Adjusted for the one-off 7.8m IEEPA/SCOTUS tariff reclaim - which must sit in H2, since H1 reported a straight 6.0m tariff cost with no reclaim - H2 core operating profit is ~111.2m vs 113.7m, roughly -2.2% YoY on +5.1% revenue, and the whole 69.5->71.1% gross-margin expansion was an H1 event plus a non-recurring credit. FY27 then carries ~8.8m of INCREMENTAL tariff (c.13m gross, no reclaim; ~27p, -4.3% of EPS) on an estimate GAW struck on 28-Jul, four days before the ~01-Aug Section-122 substitution. VALUATION GATE FAILS: 30.58x trailing = the 64th percentile of GAW's own 7-year band (n=85 month-ends x eight RNS-verified EPS prints; min 14.8 / p25 24.1 / median 27.6 / p75 32.8 / max 54.6), and 34.3x on core-only EPS (556.2p) for a ~15% core grower = PEG ~2.2. TINA does not license paying above the own-history median for a year that exits at -0.6% EPS. PATH IS LATE: +38.3% off a 52w low that is 9-10 months old, only -14.3% off an all-time high set six weeks ago. AND THE SEED EVIDENCE IS NOT UN-PRICED: the stock jumped +6.5% on 24-Jun-2026 on ~4x volume into the new-slate announcements, ran to 22,260p, and has given all of it back on the actual licensing print (-2.4% on results day, -6.0% over the five sessions since). HONESTY GRADE: GAW IS CLEAN - every component is disclosed plainly, tariffs are explicitly refused as an exceptional item ('Unlike some companies...'), and the licensing decline is volunteered by the CEO in his own words. The takeaway-vs-data divergence here is between the PITCH and the data, not between the issuer's marketing and its data - the error is in the seed thesis, not in Games Workshop. This is a HIGH-QUALITY REJECT: 196% core ROCE, zero external borrowings, 71.1% gross margin, opex held at exactly 32.0% of revenue, 182.9m net cash built AFTER 160.1m of dividends, FY27 dividends declared to date GBP 2.30 vs 1.40 (+64%) at a ~3.0% run-rate yield received with 0% UK withholding. A name to own on a real de-rate. There isn't one today - edge is +1.2% of price and +3.2pp of bull probability, inside the noise.
